facts.text: ALSEP Central Station was deployed at Taurus-Littrow during Apollo 17 in 1972.

Apollo 17's experiment suite — the most advanced of all Apollo packages. Included a lunar seismic profiling experiment, gravimeter, atmospheric composition experiment, and surface electrical properties experiment.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Its lunar seismic profiling experiment used explosive charges to map subsurface geology, and its gravimeter detected the first evidence of free oscillations of the Moon.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Taurus-Littrow.
The most advanced ALSEP package deployed; operated until NASA shut down all ALSEP stations on 30 September 1977.
